name: Diff Checker
title: Free Diff Checker & Text Comparison | PSDevTool
description: Compare two versions of text or code online. Inspect highlighted additions, deletions and edits with a side-by-side diff in PSDevTool.
intro: Find what changed between an original document and a revised version. Diff Checker provides editable comparison panes, highlighted changes and formatting controls for code and structured text.
features: Compare original and modified text side by side.
Inspect added, removed and changed content with syntax highlighting.
Adjust whitespace, wrapping and comparison settings for your task.
steps: Paste the original text into the left pane and the modified text into the right.
Choose formatting or comparison settings when needed, then select Compare.
Review highlighted differences and navigate between changes.

faq.question: What can I compare?
faq.answer: Use plain text, source code, JSON, XML or YAML. For local files and directory contents, use File & Folder Diff.

faq.question: Does formatting change a comparison?
faq.answer: Yes. Whitespace and formatting can create differences. Review the formatting and whitespace options before deciding whether a change is meaningful.

name: JSON & YAML
title: JSON Formatter, Validator & YAML Converter | PSDevTool
description: Format and validate JSON, inspect nested data and array lengths, and convert JSON to XML or YAML. Explore tree, table and graph views online.
intro: Make nested JSON easier to read, validate and explore. JSON Studio combines a syntax-colored source editor with parsed views, code folding and array-length hints. Conversion modes help move between JSON, XML, YAML and environment text.
features: Format or minify valid JSON and inspect parsing errors.
Expand nested objects, view arrays as tables, and inspect array item counts.
Convert JSON and XML/YAML in either direction using the conversion controls.
steps: Paste JSON into the source editor and check the validation status.
Select Format, or switch to Tree, Table or Graph to explore the structure.
Open a conversion mode when needed and copy or export the result.

faq.question: Can I see the length of nested JSON arrays?
faq.answer: Yes. Valid arrays have non-editable item-count hints, including nested and empty arrays. The hints do not become part of copied JSON.

faq.question: Can I expand and collapse code?
faq.answer: Use the gutter arrows or Fold/Unfold controls. Parsed tree nodes also expand independently. Invalid JSON needs to be corrected before parsed views and counts can update.

name: File & Folder Diff
title: Compare Files & Folders Online | PSDevTool
description: Compare local files or folder contents and inspect additions, deletions and changed files. Open individual text differences in PSDevTool.
intro: Review local versions without manually checking every file. File & Folder Diff compares two sets of files and lets you inspect changed text content in a comparison view.
features: Choose files or folder contents from both versions.
Identify additions, removals and modified files.
Inspect supported text-file differences in the editor.
steps: Select the original files or directory contents.
Select the modified files or directory contents.
Open a changed file to inspect its comparison and review the result.

faq.question: Can every binary file be compared as text?
faq.answer: No. Text differences are useful for readable source and text documents. Binary files may not have a meaningful line-by-line comparison.

faq.question: Are local files uploaded for comparison?
faq.answer: The comparison is processed in your browser. The page can still make external requests for application resources, analytics or advertising.

name: API Desk
title: Online API Client & OpenAPI Explorer | PSDevTool
description: Build HTTP requests, inspect API responses, import cURL and explore OpenAPI specifications. Choose direct requests or an explicit optional proxy.
intro: Build and inspect HTTP requests from a browser-based workspace. API Desk includes request methods, parameters, headers, bodies and authentication controls, plus cURL and OpenAPI workflows.
features: Configure a request and inspect status, timing, headers and response data.
Import cURL commands and work with saved collections and history.
Explore OpenAPI specifications and send endpoints to the API client.
steps: Enter the request URL and choose its HTTP method.
Configure parameters, headers, authentication and body as required.
Select Send and inspect the response or the connection error.

faq.question: Why can a browser request fail while cURL works?
faq.answer: Browsers enforce CORS rules. Check the endpoint and its CORS configuration. The optional corsproxy.io setting forwards the request through that third-party service.

faq.question: Where are collections and history stored?
faq.answer: API Desk stores collections and request history locally in this browser. Requests contact your chosen endpoint, or the optional proxy when you enable it.

name: HAR Viewer
title: HAR File Viewer & Network Waterfall | PSDevTool
description: Inspect HTTP Archive files with a network waterfall, request timing, headers and payloads. Analyze browser network captures locally in PSDevTool.
intro: Explore a browser network capture to understand requests and timing. HAR Viewer turns an HTTP Archive into an inspectable request list and waterfall rather than a large raw JSON document.
features: Open an HTTP Archive exported from browser developer tools.
Inspect request and response details, headers and timing.
Use the waterfall to investigate request ordering and delays.
steps: Export a HAR file from your browser network panel.
Open the file in HAR Viewer.
Select a request and inspect the relevant timing, headers and payload.

faq.question: What is a HAR file?
faq.answer: HAR is an HTTP Archive format used to record browser network activity. A capture can include request URLs, headers and response content, depending on how it was exported.

faq.question: Does the viewer resend recorded requests?
faq.answer: Opening and inspecting a HAR capture does not replay its requests. Use API Desk when you intentionally want to send an HTTP request.

name: JWT Debugger
title: JWT Decoder & HS256 Signature Inspector | PSDevTool
description: Decode JWT headers and claims, inspect expiration, and verify supported HS256 signatures locally. Unsupported algorithms remain explicitly unverified.
intro: Inspect a JSON Web Token and understand what it contains. JWT Debugger separates the encoded segments, decoded header and payload, expiration information and supported signature checks.
features: Decode and inspect JWT header and payload JSON.
Review time claims and expiration status.
Check HS256 signatures with a secret; other algorithms remain unverified.
steps: Paste the JWT into the token input.
Inspect the decoded header, claims and parsing status.
For an HS256 token, provide the intended secret and review its verification result.

faq.question: Does decoding a JWT prove it is trustworthy?
faq.answer: No. Decoding reveals content; it does not establish authenticity. Signature checks and your application’s issuer, audience and authorization rules are separate concerns.

faq.question: Which signature algorithms are supported?
faq.answer: This inspector supports HS256 verification. Tokens using another algorithm are labeled unsupported and are not marked verified.

name: ID Generator
title: UUID & Unique ID Generator Online | PSDevTool
description: Generate UUIDs and other supported identifiers in your browser. Explore UUID v4/v7, ULID, NanoID, Snowflake-style and MongoDB ObjectId formats.
intro: Create identifiers for examples, development and data workflows. Choose a supported format and review the generated values before using them in your application.
features: Generate supported UUID and identifier formats.
Choose quantities for batch generation.
Copy generated results for your workflow.
steps: Choose the identifier format.
Set the available generation options and quantity.
Generate the values, then copy the results.

faq.question: Are all identifier formats interchangeable?
faq.answer: No. Formats differ in length, ordering, timestamp content and intended use. Choose the format your database or application expects.

faq.question: Are generated IDs authentication secrets?
faq.answer: Identifiers and authentication credentials serve different purposes. Do not assume a sortable or timestamp-based identifier is a secure secret.

name: Architecture Lab
title: Mermaid, Architecture & Database Diagram Tools | PSDevTool
description: Create Mermaid diagrams, explore a local system-design simulator and model database relationships. Inspect connected systems in Architecture Lab.
intro: Explain a connected system with diagrams rather than scattered notes. Architecture Lab offers Mermaid source and preview, an interactive system-design model, and database relationship editing.
features: Edit Mermaid code and inspect the rendered diagram.
Explore traffic and failure settings in a local system-design simulation.
Model database tables and relationships using the ERD workspace.
steps: Choose Mermaid, System simulator or Database ERD.
Enter diagram source or configure the nodes and connections.
Inspect the result and use the export controls available for that mode.

faq.question: Are simulator metrics real production measurements?
faq.answer: No. They describe the local model and its input parameters. Use real monitoring and load testing to assess a deployed system.

faq.question: Can I edit the source of a Mermaid diagram?
faq.answer: Yes. The Mermaid mode provides a source editor and rendered preview, with controls for inspecting and exporting the diagram.

name: Regex Lab
title: Regex Tester & Capture Group Inspector | PSDevTool
description: Test regular expressions online with match highlighting, capture groups and pattern presets. Inspect JavaScript regex behavior in PSDevTool.
intro: Check a regular expression against representative text before using it in code. Regex Lab highlights matches and exposes groups so you can understand what the pattern captures.
features: Validate pattern syntax and inspect highlighted matches.
Review capture groups and matching details.
Start with presets and adjust the pattern and flags.
steps: Enter a pattern and choose the relevant flags.
Paste sample text, including matching and non-matching cases.
Inspect highlighted matches and capture groups, then refine the pattern.

faq.question: Will a pattern behave identically in every language?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Regex engines differ. This browser tool tests JavaScript regex behavior, so check the target language’s rules before copying a pattern.

faq.question: Why does a pattern match more than expected?
faq.answer: Check flags, greedy quantifiers, anchors and your test text. Capture-group output can help reveal which section of the pattern consumed the text.

name: PDF Studio
title: PDF Tools & Word to PDF Converter | PSDevTool
description: Merge and split PDF files, convert images or Word documents to PDF, and use browser-based document workflows in PSDevTool PDF Studio.
intro: Prepare documents using the available PDF workflows. PDF Studio combines merging, splitting and conversion tools so you can select an operation and work with local documents.
features: Merge PDF files and review their order.
Extract pages or split documents using the available options.
Convert images or Word documents to PDF in the browser.
steps: Choose the document operation.
Add your files and review the operation’s settings.
Run the operation, inspect the result and download the output.

faq.question: Will every Word document keep exactly the same layout?
faq.answer: Complex fonts, pagination and document features can render differently in a browser. Review the converted output before sharing or printing it.

faq.question: Do file operations require a PSDevTool upload server?
faq.answer: Local document processing runs in your browser. Some document resources may load externally, and the hosted page includes other third-party requests.

name: Image Studio
title: Image Crop, Resize & Compression Tools | PSDevTool
description: Crop, resize, rotate, flip, compress and convert images in your browser. Preview your changes and export the result with PSDevTool Image Studio.
intro: Prepare an image for the size and format you need. Image Studio brings crop, dimensions, transforms and export controls into a single browser workspace.
features: Crop images using an interactive selection and aspect-ratio options.
Resize, rotate or flip the image.
Adjust export format and compression settings.
steps: Add an image from your device.
Adjust crop, dimensions or transforms and inspect the preview.
Choose export settings and download the output.

faq.question: Can compression change image quality?
faq.answer: Yes. Lossy formats trade image detail for smaller files. Inspect the preview and exported result when changing quality settings.

faq.question: How is Base64 different from image compression?
faq.answer: Base64 is a text representation of binary data and can increase its size. Use Image Studio to change dimensions or compression, and Image Base64 when you need a data URL.

name: Time Zones
title: Time Zone & Unix Timestamp Converter | PSDevTool
description: Convert Unix timestamps, inspect dates and compare times across time zones. Check seconds versus milliseconds with PSDevTool’s time utilities.
intro: Translate machine timestamps into readable dates and compare times between locations. Check the timestamp unit and selected zone to avoid confusing the same instant with different local clock times.
features: Work with Unix epoch timestamps and readable dates.
Compare selected time zones.
Inspect UTC and local-time representations.
steps: Enter a timestamp or choose the relevant time workflow.
Confirm whether the timestamp uses seconds or milliseconds.
Select time zones and review the converted dates.

faq.question: Why is my timestamp producing an unexpected date?
faq.answer: One common cause is mixing seconds and milliseconds. Also check the selected time zone and whether the input represents UTC or local time.

faq.question: Do daylight-saving changes matter?
faq.answer: Yes. A location’s UTC offset can vary by date. Use a named time zone and the intended date rather than assuming a fixed offset for the entire year.

name: Image Base64
title: Image to Base64 & Base64 to Image Converter | PSDevTool
description: Convert an image to a Base64 data URL or decode image data in your browser. Copy a data URL and preview the decoded image with PSDevTool.
intro: Move between an image file and its text representation. Image Base64 helps create data URLs for development and inspect encoded image content.
features: Encode an image file into Base64 or a data URL.
Decode supported Base64 image data for preview.
Copy the representation needed for your development workflow.
steps: Choose whether to encode an image or decode text.
Add the image or paste the encoded input.
Inspect the preview and copy or download the available output.

faq.question: Does Base64 make an image smaller?
faq.answer: No. Base64 represents binary data as text and typically adds overhead. Resize or compress the image first if you need a smaller asset.

faq.question: Why might encoded text fail to decode as an image?
faq.answer: Check that the input is complete, correctly encoded and actually contains supported image data. A data URL’s media type should match the content.

name: Markup Studio
title: HTML, XML, Markdown & SQL Formatter | PSDevTool
description: Preview HTML and Markdown, format XML and SQL, and inspect structured markup in your browser with PSDevTool Markup Studio.
intro: Improve the readability of markup and queries before copying them into another workflow. Markup Studio combines source editing with formatting and the preview modes available for each language.
features: Preview HTML in an isolated browser frame.
Work with Markdown and formatted XML.
Format SQL using the supported dialect settings.
steps: Choose the source language or preview mode.
Paste your markup or query and select the relevant formatting options.
Inspect the output and copy the result.

faq.question: Does formatting SQL prove the query is correct?
faq.answer: No. Formatting improves layout; it does not validate your schema, permissions or query results. Test queries against the intended database safely.

faq.question: Is a preview identical to my production website?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. A preview runs in its own context and may not include your site’s styles, resources or runtime behavior.

name: Case Converter
title: Text Case & Naming Convention Converter | PSDevTool
description: Convert text to camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, uppercase or title case. Compare naming styles with PSDevTool Case Converter.
intro: Change text into the case or naming style your workflow expects. Case Converter is useful for labels, identifiers and consistently formatted text.
features: Convert common programming identifier styles.
Change prose capitalization such as upper, lower or title case.
Review and copy the converted text.
steps: Paste or type the input text.
Choose the target case or naming convention.
Review the result and copy it into your workflow.

faq.question: Will changing case rename symbols safely across a project?
faq.answer: No. This tool transforms text. Use your editor’s refactoring tools to rename code symbols and references throughout a project.

faq.question: Can punctuation and spacing affect the result?
faq.answer: Yes. Word boundaries and punctuation affect naming conversions. Review the output, especially for acronyms, numbers and mixed-language text.

name: DebugFlow
title: Stack Trace & Log Analyzer Online | PSDevTool
description: Inspect supported logs and stack traces, explore frames and context, and review rule-based investigation suggestions with PSDevTool DebugFlow.
intro: Turn a long log or stack trace into a more inspectable structure. DebugFlow extracts supported frames and context and offers rule-based suggestions for further investigation.
features: Explore supported C#/.NET, Java, Python and Node.js examples.
Inspect frames, extracted context and an inferred call chain.
Copy a report or download the analysis as JSON.
steps: Paste your log or choose a sample.
Inspect the detected information and switch between analysis views.
Review suggested checks against your code and runtime evidence before exporting the report.

faq.question: Does the tool prove the root cause of an incident?
faq.answer: No. Suggestions are derived from the supplied text and parsing rules. Verify them against application code, configuration and runtime observations.

faq.question: Is the displayed call flow a complete execution trace?
faq.answer: No. It is inferred from the stack trace. Async work, concurrent requests and omitted frames can make actual execution differ.

name: Geo Distance
title: Latitude & Longitude Distance Calculator | PSDevTool
description: Calculate distance between coordinates, place map pins and compare direct and optional driving-route distances. Convert kilometers, miles and more.
intro: Compare two geographic points using latitude and longitude. Geo Distance shows coordinate pins, a direct great-circle path and an optional driving route when the public routing service can provide one.
features: Enter coordinates, place pins on the map or drag either point.
Compare direct distance, bearings and optional road-route distance.
Explore unit equivalents, batch pairs and geofence calculations.
steps: Enter valid latitude and longitude for points A and B.
Inspect the pins and direct distance on the map.
For points up to 500 km apart, optionally request a driving route and compare its result separately.

faq.question: Why is road distance different from direct distance?
faq.answer: Direct distance follows a geographic path across Earth’s surface. Roads follow available connections and may detour; route endpoints may snap to nearby roads.

faq.question: Are maps and routing free to use?
faq.answer: The tool uses OpenStreetMap tiles and an optional OSRM public routing service without a paid API key. Those services require internet and may be unavailable; direct calculations run locally.

name: Measure Lab
title: Unit Converter, Geometry & Algebra Calculator | PSDevTool
description: Convert 119 units across 17 measurement categories with optional 3D illustrations. Explore geometry, algebra and visible formulas in PSDevTool.
intro: Make a measurement easier to understand and convert. Measure Lab pairs numeric results with optional 3D illustrations, and includes geometry and algebra workspaces with formulas you can inspect.
features: Convert compatible units across 17 measurement categories.
Explore 15 geometry shapes and six algebra tools.
Use an optional interactive 3D illustration and inspect the applicable formulas.
steps: Choose a measurement category, then enter a value and select source and target units.
Read the conversion and inspect its formula or equivalent units.
Switch to Geometry or Algebra for the relevant calculation, or hide 3D to focus on the numbers.

faq.question: Can kilograms be converted directly to liters?
faq.answer: Not without knowing the material’s density. Mass and volume are different dimensions. Choose compatible units within a category for direct conversions.

faq.question: Do the 3D illustrations limit the result?
faq.answer: No. Each illustration has a stated display range. Numeric conversions can exceed that range; the illustration may reach its visual limit. Results use floating-point arithmetic and are rounded for display.

name: URL Tools
title: URL Encoder, Decoder & Query Parser | PSDevTool
description: Encode or decode URL text and inspect query parameters in your browser. Work with URL components using PSDevTool URL Tools.
intro: Inspect and transform a URL without manually reading every escaped character. URL Tools helps encode or decode text and understand query-string parameters.
features: Encode and decode URL text.
Inspect URL components and query parameters.
Copy transformed values for your workflow.
steps: Choose the encoding, decoding or query-inspection workflow.
Paste the URL or relevant text component.
Review escaped characters and parameters before copying the output.

faq.question: Why do some characters appear as percent codes?
faq.answer: URLs use percent encoding for certain characters and bytes. Encoding a whole URL and encoding an individual parameter can require different handling.

faq.question: Does decoding a URL make its destination safe?
faq.answer: No. Decoding makes text readable. Inspect the destination and parameter values separately before visiting or sending a URL.
